lesson.menu_desc: Life before and after retirement, and the party question: so, what do you do? -- 13 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- Then and Now
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Eglis Roberto | Lesson 5 -- Then and Now

listenings.text: I worked for thirty-eight years. I used to wake up at five, and I would be in the office before seven. For years, I would come home after my kids were asleep. Now I am retired, and people keep asking me: so, what are you doing now? Are you not bored? And I say no. I am doing nothing, and I am very good at it. It took me a few months to get used to it. At first, I felt guilty every morning. Now I am used to slow mornings, long lunches and a nap after lunch. I have earned it.

When I retired, I did not want to stop. I wanted to start. I used to be an accountant, and I would spend my days with numbers. At sixty-two, I signed up for a sailing course. The first week was terrible. I was not used to the wind, the ropes and the noise. But I got used to it, and two years later I crossed the Atlantic as crew on a small boat. So when people ask me what I do, I say: I sail. Retirement is not the end of your story. It is the first free chapter.
